articles.headline: Source: Niners signing veteran receiver Cooks to practice squad
articles.description: The Niners are signing free agent wideout Brandin Cooks to their practice squad, a source told ESPN on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ナイナーズがベテランWRクックスと練習生契約へ
articles.descriptionJa: ナイナーズがフリーエージェントのワイドレシーバー、ブランディン・クックスと練習生契約を結ぶと、関係者が火曜日にESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Free agent wide receiver Brandin Cooks is signing with the San Francisco 49ers' practice squad, initially to get up to speed for games, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Tuesday.

Cooks, 32, joins a Niners team that has lost wideouts Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson to injury this season. Meanwhile, veteran wide receiver Mike Evans will need to be managed this week with a hip injury.

Cooks was the 20th pick in the 2014 draft by the Saints out of Oregon State, and he spent the first three years of his career with New Orleans. He returned to the Saints in 2025 but was waived in November after he requested his release. Cooks then joined the Buffalo Bills for the remainder of the campaign.

Cooks was part of a controversial call that ultimately played a large role in ending the Bills' season. In a divisional round playoff game at the Denver Broncos, a downfield pass from quarterback Josh Allen in overtime appeared to be initially caught by Cooks, but the ball was then taken away as Cooks came to the ground. The play was ultimately ruled an interception by Broncos cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian. The Bills never got the ball back, and then-coach Sean McDermott loudly expressed his displeasure in the officiating process after the game.

Cooks also has played for the New England Patriots, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Dallas Cowboys. He has competed in two Super Bowls -- LII and LIII -- with the Patriots and the Rams, losing both.

He has 734 career receptions for 9,811 yards and 62 total touchdowns in 12 seasons.

articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, with Aaron Wiggins' trade to the Atlanta Hawks on June 22 the first move in what has already been a frenzied offseason.

The big news came a day before the NBA draft, when Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded by the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat in a blockbuster. There was another big trade the morning after the draft, as the Charlotte Hornets shipped LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves. And the trades haven't stopped since.

I'm grading every trade this offseason, including draft deals, and breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the on-court impact and ages of involved players, the cost in terms of draft picks and future financial implications, and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win the championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Latest buzz | FA signing grades | Trade machine

Depth charts | Offseason guides | Draft coverage

Sept. 22: Hawks send Hield, Nembhard to Hornets for Finney-Smith

Charlotte Hornets get: G Buddy Hield, G Ryan Nembhard, cash considerations

Atlanta Hawks get: F Dorian Finney-Smith

Grade for Hawks: B+

For the Hawks, this swap of reserve wings is primarily about resolving a roster crunch, as they trade two players -- including backup guard Nembhard, whom they had initially acquired alongside Luguentz Dort in an earlier trade -- for one.

That fix comes at a minor price, as Finney-Smith will earn $14.2 million this season, compared with $11.8 million combined for Hield and Nembhard. (Finney-Smith and Hield are both nominally signed for additional years, but for zero guaranteed money.) The Hawks are reportedly sending cash to Charlotte in this deal, as well.

But this deal is smart business for the Hawks because it gives them another potential two-way contributor on the wing, as they build out a fearsome defensive rotation. Hield doesn't fit that mold, and he never seemed to find his footing in Atlanta. He arrived from Golden State in the Kristaps Porzingis trade last February but played just 51 minutes over the rest of the regular season, as the Hawks enjoyed their late-season surge without him.

Finney-Smith, meanwhile, was far worse than Hield last season, as he averaged only 3.3 points per game and made 27% of his 3s after returning from ankle surgery. That disappointing level of production incentivized Houston to trade him to Charlotte earlier this offseason, in a salary dump that brought the Hornets three second-round picks.

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as they assess attacking options ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The 30-year-old is being considered as an experienced option should Joshua Zirkzee depart, while United remain committed to Benjamin Šeško despite his recent injury issues. Dortmund are reluctant to let Guirassy leave, but his contract has less than two years remaining, which could force their hand. Meanwhile, The Sun reports that United are targeting Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic as a replacement for JJ Gabriel. 

- Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 20-year-old Netherlands U21 international has registered four assists in seven Eredivisie appearances this season, with all three clubs continuing to track his progress following summer interest. A January move remains an option depending on formal approaches, after Nottingham Forest and AS Roma previously submitted offers of around €20 million that came to nothing.

- Barcelona are monitoring Athletico Paranaense center back Arthur Dias, as per Mundo Deportivo. Barca's head of scouting, João Amaral, reportedly watched the 19-year-old against Bahia, with Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Atlético Madrid also among his admirers. The left-footed defender, who earned a call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad, has a transfer value of around €30 million and after Spurs previously had a €21 million offer for 80% of his economic rights rejected.

- Tottenham Hotspur will not pursue a move for free-agent Mauro Icardi, Football Insider has revealed. The 33-year-old striker has been available since leaving Galatasaray in July, but Spurs are wary of his wage demands and lack of Premier League experience. Serie A is considered the likeliest destination for the former Sampdoria, Inter Milan and PSG star, with Lazio among several interested Italian clubs.

- Roma are interested in signing free-agent Raphaël Guerreiro, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The 32-year-old Portugal international left back has re-emerged as an option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini as a natural left-footed alternative on the flank, while Olympiacos are also interested in the former Bayern Munich defender.

articles.headline: Mets remove interim manager tag, hire Andy Green to 3-year deal
articles.description: The Mets have removed the interim tag from manager Andy Green, hiring him to a three-year deal through the 2029 season, it was announced Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: メッツ、アンディ・グリーン監督代行の「代行」を外し3年契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: メッツは火曜日、アンディ・グリーン監督代行の「代行」を外し、2029年シーズンまでの3年契約を結んだと発表した。
articles.body:
The New York Mets removed the interim tag from manager Andy Green and agreed to a three-year contract with him to remain at the helm through the 2029 season, the team announced Tuesday.

The decision comes with six games remaining in a season that will go down as a monumental disappointment despite concluding on a high note.

The Mets carried World Series aspirations going into the season with the second-highest payroll in the majors after failing to reach the playoffs in 2025. But significant injuries, including to Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor, and widespread underperformance throughout the roster derailed their season early.

New York was 34-47 when manager Carlos Mendoza was fired and Green was named interim manager in late June. Since then, they're 37-38 under Green and have held their own against a variety of playoff-caliber opponents in the second half after trading eight major leaguers in the weeks leading into the trade deadline.

Within the disappointment, several young players have developed into foundational pillars for the future, led by right-hander Nolan McLean and outfielder Carson Benge, both of whom are expected to finish in the top four in National League Rookie of the Year voting.

"Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," Mets owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement. "Over the last several months he has brought discipline, accountability and positivity to the clubhouse, attributes we were seeking in our next manager."

Green, 49, was the Mets' vice president of player development when he was asked by president of baseball operations David Stearns to replace Mendoza. At the time, and through the summer, it was presumed to be a temporary move as Green, citing his desire to spend time with his family, insisted he wanted to return to the front office after the season -- and Mets officials said they would oblige.

All along, however, Mets officials hoped Green would change his mind and entertain the chance to remain the permanent manager.

"I love this," Green said Sunday before the Mets' final home game of the season. "I've always loved this. I think I've said this before, [I've spent] 27 years in professional baseball now, 24 of them in a uniform in some capacity. I've basically been wearing a uniform since I was 4 years old going to my brother's T-ball games. It's home; the dugout's always been home to me. So I love it. I've loved these guys and the challenge that comes with it.

"I've also loved the opportunity to be invested in player development as well. I think that's the healthiest way to go through life. Just be fully present where you are at the time and enjoy that."

Green previously managed the San Diego Padres for nearly four seasons starting in 2016. He went 274-366 before he was fired near the end of the 2019 campaign. He then spent four years as the Chicago Cubs' bench coach before joining the Mets' organization in November 2023.

articles.headline: Sources: Hawks trade Hield, Nembhard to Hornets for Finney-Smith
articles.description: The Hawks are sending Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ホークスがヒールドとネムハードをホーネッツへトレード、フィニー＝スミスを獲得
articles.descriptionJa: 情報筋がESPNに語ったところによると、ホークスはバディ・ヒールド、ライアン・ネムハード、および金銭をシャーロット・ホーネッツへ放出し、ドリアン・フィニー＝スミスを獲得する。
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks are trading Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

The Hornets are expected to waive Nembhard as part of the trade, sources told Charania. The Hawks create a $2.1 million trade exception and the Hornets likely create a $4.5 million trade exception with the deal, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Hield landed in Atlanta in the trade that sent Kristaps Porzingis to the Golden State Warriors but appeared in just seven games for the Hawks last season; the sharpshooting guard is due around $9.5 million this season and has a player option for just over $10 million for 2027-28.

 

Finney-Smith was acquired by Charlotte in a trade with the Houston Rockets earlier in the offseason. The veteran wing missed the first two months of the season for Houston and has three years left on his $53 million contract, including a player option for 2028-29.

Nembhard, an undrafted rookie last season for Dallas, was acquired by the Hawks in a three-team trade that sent Zaccharie Risacher to the Mavericks and Luguentz Dort back to Atlanta from Oklahoma City.

Nembhard, 23, averaged 6.6 points and 5.3 assists in 19.5 minutes per game last season.

articles.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Walker, Shough on the rise while Maye, McConkey fall
articles.description: Need a quick free agent pickup -- or roster overhaul -- after Week 2? These rankings are designed to help.
articles.headlineJa: 残りシーズンのランキング：ウォーカーとショウが上昇、メイとマコンキーは下落
articles.descriptionJa: 第2週を終えてフリーエージェントの補強やロースターの刷新が必要ですか？このランキングがその手助けとなります。
articles.body:
Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. 

Quarterback

Rankings changes: Wow. Serious injuries to the top two selections from the 2024 draft and a late 2025 first rounder are the story, as fantasy managers will miss the Bears' Caleb Williams (hamstring), Commanders' Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Giants' Jaxson Dart (knee) for an undetermined length of time. Each was among our top 10 QBs. Perhaps the mercurial Williams will return far sooner, so he remains in QB2 range in these rankings, but the risk of reinjury is high. Dart may be lost for the season. Backups Jameis Winston and Marcus Mariota enter the rankings, and they may be playing for months.

With three passers dropping in the rankings, nearly everyone else rises. The 49ers' Brock Purdy, Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes, Saints' Tyler Shough and Lions' Jared Goff are all in the top 10. The Panthers' Bryce Young rises into safer QB2 territory, with room for more. The Patriots' Drake Maye, last year's No. 2 QB scorer, remains in the top 10, but perhaps not for long after two disappointing outings totaling 17.84 points. The Rams' Matthew Stafford rebounds from Australia and is No. 11. It is quite amazing how quickly fantasy value changes in the NFL.

Running back

Rankings changes: Volume is king, and no running back earned more in Week 2 than the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III. Will he stay healthy? That was an offseason concern, but so far he looks awesome and he continues rising into the top 10. For those that want Walker at No. 1 ... c'mon, we are not there yet. Walker versus Bijan Robinson? It feels premature, though Robinson does drop a spot behind Jonathan Taylor to No. 3. Praise Walker, but if a Robinson investor offers him for Walker, do it.

Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is among big risers at running back, though we lack confirmation of solid volume moving ahead (same with the Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson). The Buccaneers' Bucky Irving and Panthers' Chuba Hubbard rise to RB2 status, as their reported timeshares appear to be rather one-sided. Aaron Jones Sr. is healthy and seeing volume. Don't forget about the Saints' Alvin Kamara and Seahawks' Zach Charbonnet, and watch for injury updates on the Eagles' Saquon Barkley.

Wide receiver

Rankings changes: Many star receivers delivered in Week 2, but the rankings movement at this position happened in the late-WR2 range, as the Panthers' Jalen Coker, Packers' Christian Watson, Broncos' Jaylen Waddle, Jaguars' Parker Washington and Browns' Denzel Boston continue to add value.
